findings.reason: The protected query computes the right rows but adds ORDER BY q.id, q.year even though the authenticated source explicitly permits any order. That sort has no semantic purpose and can add O(Q log Q) work beyond the branch's required O(P+Q) bound. The candidate removes only the sort, retaining the same composite-key left join and COALESCE projection.

Queries drives a LEFT JOIN on the complete (id, year) key. Each requested pair therefore produces exactly one row, a match supplies its unique stored npv, and an absent match becomes zero through COALESCE. Unrequested NPV rows cannot enter the result, equal IDs in different years remain independent, stored zero remains zero, and empty Queries yields no rows.

An independent Python dictionary oracle mapped each NPV composite key and independently evaluated every Queries key. It, the candidate, protected app query, exact immutable native query, a separately written CASE-based left join, and a correct de-indexed correlated lookup agreed under unordered comparison on all eight visible cases and all three benchmark tiers.

Seed 1421 generated 5,000 deterministic source-valid databases totaling 45,959 NPV rows and 47,996 Queries rows. Coverage included 1,250 all-matched, 2,246 all-missing, 1,443 mixed, 93 empty-NPV, 61 empty-Queries, 643 stored-zero, 4,232 negative-value, 4,401 unrequested-value, 4,503 repeated-ID-across-years, 4,714 signed-or-zero-key, and 4,909 shuffled databases; every implementation matched the oracle.

Across three real-test repetitions, the candidate passed all eight ordinary cases, all three benchmark outputs, and scaling with extra growth exponent -0.02 through +0.01 and largest-tier ratio 0.95x through 0.99x. The protected query and independent join also passed every gate. The de-indexed correlated lookup passed every output but failed only scaling each time, with relative growth exponent +0.29 through +0.31 over the +0.15 limit.

All three benchmark tiers remain hidden and performance-only, retain their original workloads and expected rows, use positive unique sizes 32, 128, and 512 for a 16x span, and define size consistently as P+Q. Their validators now honor the source's unrestricted result order; this calibration defect was the only benchmark edit. Correct de-indexed correlation reliably fails only the scaling verdict.
